title: हाइकु कविताको रचनाविधान : नेपाली परम्परा र विकास {Composition of Haiku Poetry: Nepali Tradition and Development}
nepali: जापानी साहित्यको इतिहासमा सन् १६०३ देखि १८६८ सम्मको समयलाई इदोयुग भनिन्छ । यस समयमा जापानमा हाइकाई नामका लघु कविता लेख्ने परम्परा रहेको थियो भने एकतिस अक्षरमा संरचित हुने होक्कु पनि लेखिन्थ्यो । होक्कुको पहिलो पङ्क्तिका तीन हरफलाई केन्द्र मानेर कविता साहित्यमा स्वतन्त्र विधा स्वीकार गर्दा सत्र अक्षर भएको त्रिपदीहाइकु कविताको जन्म भएको हो । माचुओ बासोले जापानी वाङ्मयमा विस्तार गरेको हाइकु कविताको संरचना विधान स्वीकार गरी नेपाली साहित्यमा शङ्कर लामिछानेले वि.सं २०१९ मा रूपरेखा पत्रिकामा सूर्योदय शीर्षकमा सर्वप्रथम हाइकु प्रकाशन गरेका थिए । वैदिक वाङ्मयदेखि नै त्रिपदी संरचना भएका कविताका बारेमा चर्चा भएको पाइए पनि यिनलाई हाइकु स्वीकार गरिएको थिएन । नेपाली साहित्यमा हाइकुको प्रारम्भ भएको समयदेखि वर्तमान समयसम्म हाइकु विषयक चर्चा एवम् तिनको सर्वेक्षण गरी हाइकु कविताको रचनाविधान र परम्परा पहिल्याउने अभीष्ट यस लेखमा राखिएको छ ।
american_english: In the history of Japanese literature, the period from 1603 to 1868 AD is called the Edo period. During this time, there was a tradition in Japan of writing short poems called haikai, while hokku structured in thirty-one syllables was also written. Taking the three lines of the first stanza of hokku as the focus and accepting it as an independent genre in poetic literature gave birth to the three-line, seventeen-syllable haiku poem. Adopting the structural rules of haiku poetry expanded in Japanese literature by Matsuo Basho, Shankar Lamichhane first published haiku in Nepali literature in the journal Rooprekha under the title "Suryodaya" in 2019 BS. Even though discussions about poems with a three-line structure are found dating back to Vedic literature, these were not accepted as haiku. The ambition of this article is to trace the compositional structure and tradition of haiku poetry by surveying discussions regarding haiku from the time haiku began in Nepali literature up to the present day.
british_english: In the history of Japanese literature, the period from 1603 to 1868 is known as the Edo period. During this era, there was a tradition in Japan of composing short poems called haikai, whilst hokku structured in thirty-one syllables was also written. Taking the three lines of the opening stanza of hokku as the central focus and acknowledging it as an independent genre in poetic literature gave rise to the three-line, seventeen-syllable haiku poem. Adopting the structural conventions of haiku poetry developed in Japanese literature by Matsuo Basho, Shankar Lamichhane first published haiku in Nepalese literature in the journal Rooprekha under the title "Suryodaya" in 2019 BS. Although discussions concerning poems with a tripartite structure can be found as far back as Vedic literature, these were not acknowledged as haiku. The aim of this paper is to trace the compositional rules and tradition of haiku poetry by surveying discussions on haiku from the inception of haiku in Nepalese literature up to the present day.
